title: Continuous perioperative infusion of cefazolin to reduce surgical wound infections in neuro & cardiac surgery
summary: It is standard medical practice to administer antibiotics during a surgery to prevent surgical site infections. This is normally carried out by the anesthesiology department in the form of single doses at fixed times during the operation. The Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine at Essen University Hospital is now investigating whether changing the administration of antibiotics from administration at fixed times to a continuous infusion can further reduce the surgical site infection rate. For this purpose, small amounts of blood are taken at certain times during the operation via vascular catheters that are already in place (such as the “arterial line”) and the concentration of the antibiotic used in the blood is measured. Initially, the measurements are carried out using the current standard (single doses at fixed times) and the surgical site infections are monitored. After changing the standard to a continuous infusion, blood samples are taken at the same times and in the same way to measure the concentration. In addition, the incidence of surgical site infections is also recorded in this group as a quality assurance measure. The blood taken is processed pseudonymously (i.e. staff processing the blood sample cannot draw any conclusions about the identity of the patient). Within the scope of the study, data that is routinely collected during medical care will be used. These include, for example, certain laboratory values (such as the C-reactive protein “CRP” as an inflammation marker or creatinine, which can be used as a laboratory value to estimate kidney function), which are routinely determined by the attending physicians after the operation. These laboratory values are collected by the attending physicians at regular intervals. As part of the study, we evaluate these laboratory values up to 30 days after the operation or until the patient is discharged. The medical treatment is not affected by the study at any time and the study does not result in any additional costs for the individual patient. We do not require any further information from the patient afterwards and no additional study-related blood samples are taken after the surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective surgery, planned duration >150 min
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency surgery, revision surgery, existing infection with already therapeutic antibiotic use, history of penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis, severe exanthema, shortness of breath) with the consequence of not using cephalosporins for antibiotic prophylaxis, acute or chronic kidney damage
